## 1. Their trajectory, stage by stage

| Stage | Their move | What it gets them | Our counter, without springing the trap | Warning sign |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Now to Dec | Push the pending motion (19 May 2026) to admit Gloria's excluded affidavit, so she can testify to a 1980s down payment first-hand | A first-hand witness inside the class | Our Comment-Opposition stands. If she is admitted, her own S43 (no contact with the owners) helps us. Her account has no receipt, and her family paid as "Occupant" every month to 2014. Her amounts conflict: ₱3,000 in the 1980s, "by 1992," and ₱20,000 in 2005 to Salvador. | An order on the motion; a notice that she will testify by videoconference |
| Now to Dec | Pull the guardianship petition from RTC Branch 41. It says the co-owners, "by reason of their advanced age," are "unable to effectively manage" their property | An attack on Exh. A, on Jonathan's authority, and on Patricia's competence as a witness | The petition cannot be changed now, so we answer it. A petition is an allegation, not a finding, and competence is presumed. Read whole, its ground is "advanced age, prolonged residence abroad, and the practical inability to personally attend" to acts in the Philippines: inability to be present, not inability of mind. Her own recent sworn acts show her competence: the Makati affidavits of February 2023 and the apostilled SPA of November 2025 (Exh. A). Her live testimony by videoconference shows it best. We never raise the petition ourselves. | Ramos cites or subpoenas the guardianship record |
| Any time, even on appeal | Jurisdiction: nullity of a deed and cancellation of a title as actions "incapable of pecuniary estimation," for the RTC | Dismissal; years lost refiling | The main relief is recovery of ownership and possession of land, assessed at ₱257,670 (Exh. D), within BP 129 §33(3) as amended; the court took cognizance on 6 February. Counsel keeps the Supreme Court authority on assessed-value jurisdiction verified and ready [to fetch]. | A motion to dismiss, or the point raised in a memorandum |
| Any time | Cesar's estate, the vendor, is not a defendant: "indispensable party" (Rule 3 §7) | An order to join, then delay; dismissal only if we fail to comply | "Neither misjoinder nor non-joinder of parties is ground for dismissal of an action" (Rule 3 §11). Be ready to comply the same week: identify Cesar's heirs now. Salvador, their witness, is his son. | A motion, or the court's own order to join |
| After 9 Dec | Demurrer: we proved tenancy but not that Gloria never paid Llamanzares; non-consultation is hearsay; the annotated SPA allowed a sale; no revocation was annotated (Arts. 1921, 1922; PD 1529 §52; _Sarili_) | Judgment without presenting witnesses, so the trap never springs | A demurrer tests only whether we made a case. We did: paragraph 7 on its face (Exh. E); their admitted tenancy; a deed eleven years after the revocation (Exhs. F, H); their burden to prove their own good faith (_Bucton_). If it is denied, they must present evidence. If it is granted and reversed, they lose the right to present it (Rule 33 §1). | A motion filed within the period after we rest |
| Jan to Mar 2027 | Their case, in the order Ramos will argue it (Part 2) | A factual record for each defense | The lock-in on cross, and the objections in Part 3 | Witnesses dropped or substituted |
| Rebuttal | Object that Patricia and the records are our original case, not rebuttal | Consultation never proved | Every item is keyed to a transcript line it answers. If needed, ask for the "good reasons" exception (Rule 30 §5[f]). The class leg does not depend on rebuttal. | Their objection to our rebuttal affidavits |
| After judgment | Appeal to the RTC, then the CA; keep possession and the room rents meanwhile; press retention | Time and money even in defeat | Fruits from 22 August 2025 (Art. 549) and a temperate-damages figure on the record (the rents from cross); retention denied under Arts. 449 and 1678; a record exact enough to be affirmed | Notice of appeal |
